title: RATE: Causal Explainability of Reward Models with Imperfect Counterfactuals

bias_targets.methodology: Using LLMs to generate counterfactual pairs of longer and shorter texts, followed by rewrites of those rewrites, to isolate and measure the causal effect of length on reward model scores.

Rewriting evaluation texts to vary their complexity level while holding other attributes constant, then measuring the average treatment effect on reward models using the double-rewrite RATE estimator.
Generating imperfect counterfactual responses expressing either positive or negative sentiment to evaluate a reward model's causal responsiveness to sentiment, adjusting for off-target modifications.
Rewriting responses to alter their helpfulness in order to measure the reward model's sensitivity to the helpfulness attribute without being confounded by spurious correlations.

Artificially correlating off-target attributes like typos with arbitrary text features (e.g., starting with a vowel) to test whether evaluation methods can disentangle true causal effects from spurious dataset correlations.
